title: Everyday minor problems
about: Small things that go wrong at home and in everyday life: a leaking pipe, flat batteries, a twisted ankle, a power cut, keys left inside.

parts.title: Things that go wrong in houses and flats
One word, two jobs
parts.note: Багато слів цього юніту працюють і як дієслово, і як іменник. Помічай це одразу, коли записуєш нове слово.

rows: The glass cracked when I poured boiling water in.
There's a crack in the window.
There's a chip on the edge of this plate.
I bumped my head on the shelf.
He's got a bump on his forehead.
She banged her knee on the desk.
He got a nasty bang on the head.
How did you get that bruise?
I grazed my elbow on the wall.
There's a dent in the door.
I can't get this stain out.
The flood damaged hundreds of homes.
Don't forget to lock the back door.
The lock on the back door is broken.

items.meaning: liquid or gas gets out through a small hole
items.example: The pipe under the sink is **leaking** again.
more: There's water on the floor. I think the washing machine is **leaking**.
We found a small **leak** in the roof after the storm.

items.meaning: break into many pieces, often noisily
items.example: The kids kicked the ball too hard and **smashed** a window.
more: I dropped a plate and it **smashed** on the tiles.
Someone **smashed** the glass of the bus shelter last night.

items.meaning: has a thin line where it broke, but is still in one piece
items.example: This mug is **cracked**, so don't pour hot tea into it.
more: My phone screen got **cracked** when I dropped it.
There's a long **crack** in the bathroom mirror.

items.meaning: have no power left
items.example: The batteries in the remote have **run out**. I'll buy some more.
more: My phone's **dead**. Can I borrow your charger?
The torch is useless, the batteries are **dead**.
items.watchOut: «Сіли батарейки» — не sat down. Кажуть: the batteries have run out / are dead. Про телефон: my phone's dead / my phone has died.

items.meaning: a small piece has broken off the edge
items.example: Sorry, your cup's **chipped**. Let me get you another one.
more: Most of our old plates are **chipped** at the edges.
She **chipped** a tooth on a cherry stone.

items.meaning: not functioning right now
items.example: The lift **isn't working**, so we'll have to take the stairs.
more: The lights **aren't working**. There must be a power cut.
The ticket machine **isn't working** again.
items.watchOut: isn't working — не працює зараз; doesn't work — не працює взагалі, завжди (This button doesn't work).

items.meaning: a time when the electricity supply stops
items.example: We had to use candles because there was a **power cut**.
more: The whole street was dark during the **power cut**.
Charge your phone in case there's a **power cut** tonight.
items.watchOut: Не «the light was turned off» і не «light cut». Британською — a power cut, американською — a power outage.

items.meaning: becomes separated from the thing it was attached to
items.example: The handle has **come off** the kitchen drawer.
more: A button **came off** my coat on the bus.
The mirror **fell off** the wall in the night.

items.meaning: stops working (machines, cars)
items.example: Our washing machine **broke down** the other day.
more: The bus **broke down** halfway to the city.
Our old fridge finally **broke down** last summer.
items.watchOut: Техніка чи машина перестала працювати — break down. Просто broke — коли річ розбилася: the cup broke.

items.meaning: is pressed so hard that it gets damaged or loses its shape
items.example: The eggs **got crushed** at the bottom of the shopping bag.
more: My sandwich **got crushed** in my backpack.
Hold the flowers carefully or they'll **get crushed**.

items.meaning: suddenly stops working (a computer, a phone, an app)
items.example: My laptop keeps **crashing** today.
more: The app **crashed** just as I was paying.
My phone **crashed** and I lost the photo I was editing.

items.meaning: hurt it by turning it too far
items.example: She **twisted** her ankle coming down the stairs.
more: I **twisted** my wrist trying to catch the ball.
Be careful on those rocks. It's easy to **twist** an ankle.
items.watchOut: «Підвернув ногу» — I twisted my ankle. Тут нога — ankle (щиколотка), а не leg.

items.pattern: bump / bang your head on sth
items.meaning: hit part of your body on something hard by accident
items.example: I **banged** my head on the cupboard door.
more: Mind the beam. Everyone **bumps** their head on it.
He **banged** his knee against the table leg.
items.watchOut: Вдаритися об щось — bump/bang your head on або against, але не about.

items.meaning: a dark mark on your skin where you were hit
items.example: I fell off my bike and got a big **bruise** on my leg.
more: The **bruise** went from purple to yellow in a week.
I **bruise** easily. The smallest knock leaves a mark.
items.watchOut: Вимова: /bruːz/, римується з cruise. Буває і дієсловом: I bruise easily.

items.meaning: almost fall because your foot hits something
items.example: I **tripped** over the dog's lead in the hall.
more: Mind the step, don't **trip**.
She **tripped** on the edge of the carpet and spilt her tea.

items.meaning: fall to the ground
items.example: He slipped on the ice and **fell down**.
more: The little boy **fell down** and started crying.
I **fell over** in the park and everyone saw it.

items.meaning: scrape the skin so it's red and sore, with little or no blood
items.example: Kids fall off their bikes and **graze** their knees all the time.
more: It's only a **graze**. Wash it and put a plaster on.
I **grazed** my hand on the brick wall.

items.meaning: put something somewhere and forget where
items.example: I've **mislaid** my glasses. Have you seen them anywhere?
more: I'm always **mislaying** my keys.
The letter was **mislaid** and arrived a week late.
items.watchOut: lost — ширше слово. mislaid точніше: річ десь поруч, ти просто не пам'ятаєш, куди її поклав.

items.meaning: let liquid flow out of its container by accident
items.example: I **spilt** coffee all over the carpet.
more: Careful, you're going to **spill** your tea.
Someone **spilled** juice on the sofa.
items.watchOut: Пролити — spill, а не pour. Pour — лити навмисно: Can you pour me some tea?

items.meaning: a mark that is difficult to remove
items.example: Red wine leaves a **stain** that's hard to get out.
more: There's a coffee **stain** on my shirt.
Tea **stains** your teeth if you drink a lot of it.

items.meaning: water can't flow through it
items.example: The kitchen sink is **blocked** again.
more: The toilet's **blocked**. We need a plumber.
I can't breathe through my nose, it's completely **blocked**.
items.watchOut: Британською — blocked, американською — clogged. A blocked nose — закладений ніс.

items.meaning: make a small hollow in a hard surface by hitting it
items.example: I'm afraid I've **dented** your car. I'll pay for the repairs.
more: Someone left a **dent** in my car door in the car park.
The fridge got **dented** when we moved flats.

items.meaning: no longer functions
items.example: My headphones have **stopped working**. I can only hear in one ear.
more: The TV remote has **stopped working**.
The heating **stopped working** in the middle of January.

items.meaning: close a door and have no key with you to open it
items.example: The wind blew the door shut and I'd **locked myself out**.
more: Leave a spare key with a neighbour in case you **lock yourself out**.
I **locked myself out** of the car with the engine running.
items.watchOut: Не «closed myself outside». Кажуть: I've locked myself out.

items.meaning: refuses to start
items.example: The car **won't start**. I hope it's nothing serious.
more: I turned the key, but the engine **wouldn't start**.
The lawnmower **won't start** after the winter.
items.watchOut: «Не заводиться» — won't start: won't тут означає «відмовляється». Doesn't start звучить неприродно.

items.meaning: has no electrical power left (a car battery)
items.example: Perhaps the battery's **flat**. Can you give me a jump start?
more: I left the lights on all night and now the battery's **flat**.
A **flat** battery is the most common winter problem.
items.watchOut: Про акумулятор машини — flat (UK) або dead. Про телефон частіше кажуть dead.

items.pattern: a clock is slow / fast / has stopped
items.meaning: shows a time that's too early, too late, or doesn't move
items.example: The kitchen clock's ten minutes **slow**. What time do you make it?
more: No wonder I'm early. My watch is **fast**.
The clock has **stopped**. It needs a new battery.
items.watchOut: Годинник відстає — is slow, а не is late. Поспішає — is fast. What time do you make it? — «Котра у вас година?»

warmup.q: The batteries in the remote have ___.
warmup.explain: Батарейки сіли — have run out або are dead.

warmup.uk: Я захлопнув двері, а ключі залишилися всередині.
warmup.explain: Lock yourself out. Shut yourself away — усамітнитися, це про інше.
Пролити випадково — spill. Pour — лити навмисно.

warmup.q: She ___ her ankle on the stairs.
There was a ___ in the whole street.

A.q: Water is dripping from the pipe under the sink. It's ___.
We sat in the dark for two hours because of a ___.
Our washing machine ___ last week, so we're using the launderette.
A.explain: break down — про техніку; break off — відламатися; break out — спалахнути (про пожежу, війну).

B.q: I didn't see the step and ___.
B.explain: Спіткнувся — tripped. Twist і graze потребують додатка: twist your ankle, graze your knee.

B.q: I banged my arm on the door and now I've got a big ___.
B.explain: Синець після удару — a bruise. Graze — садно, коли здер шкіру.

C.q: I've ___ my glasses. They're somewhere in the house.
C.explain: Mislay — кудись подіти й не пам'ятати куди.

C.q: The car won't start. Perhaps the battery's ___.
C.explain: Сів акумулятор — the battery's flat (або dead).

C.q: Leave a spare key with a neighbour in case you ___ yourself out.
C.explain: Lock yourself out — захлопнути двері без ключів.

example.title: A Monday to forget
example.uk:
Усе почалося о шостій, коли не задзвонив будильник: сіли батарейки. Я вискочив з ліжка, спіткнувся об сумку і вдарився коліном об шафу. До сніданку в мене вже був великий синець.

Потім я пролив каву на свою єдину чисту сорочку, і пляма не відпиралася. Я перевдягнувся, грюкнув дверима і зрозумів, що ключі залишилися всередині. На щастя, у сусіда є запасний ключ.

Звісно ж, машина не заводилася — акумулятор сів. Я поїхав автобусом, і на півдорозі до міста він зламався. Коли я нарешті дістався до офісу, там вимкнули світло. Бувають дні, коли краще просто лишитися в ліжку.
example.en:
It started at six, when my alarm didn't go off: the batteries [[had run out|a4]]. I jumped out of bed, [[tripped|b4]] over my bag and [[banged|b2]] my knee on the wardrobe. By breakfast I had a big [[bruise|b3]].

Then I [[spilt|c2]] coffee on my only clean shirt, and the [[stain|c3]] wouldn't come out. I changed, slammed the door and realised I had [[locked myself out|c7]]. Luckily my neighbour has a spare key.

Of course, the car [[wouldn't start|c8]]: the battery was [[flat|c9]]. I took the bus, and halfway to the city it [[broke down|a9]]. When I finally got to the office, there was a [[power cut|a7]]. Some days you should just stay in bed.
